gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-mro: Noto Sans Mro reads dense and lofty through the middle, with generous entrances into each letter. Junegull is the odd one out, a retro display face with no thick-to-thin shading and a friendly, pinched curve that gives the pair its character.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-multani: Wire-bent and wholly retro, Junegull sets the mood with tubular letterforms and friendly pinched curves. Noto Sans Multani then steps in with a lofty x-height and an e that opens wide at its terminal, so the text feels modern next to it.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-nabatae: Contemporary in feel, Noto Sans Nabataean has lowercase that nearly matches its capitals and wide-open s curves. And Junegull gives it a foil, with closed, tube-like letters that hold their thickness through every bend, which is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-newa: Noto Sans Newa keeps a clearly open mouth on its lowercase e, with counters and bowls that stand high on the line. Junegull does the opposite job, closing its shapes into a chunky retro display look.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-ogham: Noto Sans Ogham looks surprisingly bold for a plain sans, because its lowercase bodies are so large and the gaps in the e stay wide. Over a full page it would read crisply and cleanly, with Junegull's closed letters left to the heading.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-old-hun: Approachable and wide open, Noto Sans Old Hungarian gives its a, e and s large counters that hold up even when shrunk. Junegull's closed retro letters sit above it, so the body can go small without losing clarity.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-old-nor: Noto Sans Old North Arabian forms a dense lowercase band, its terminals flaring outward like a pair of tongs. Junegull, by contrast, draws contrast-free strokes from stem to terminal, and its closed shapes make the body's open ones stand out.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-old-per: Noto Sans Old Persian reads lofty and clean, its open counters breathing into the white space around them. And Junegull handles the loud, retro display work with closed letters, while the body simply lets the words carry on.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-old-sog: Junegull's line is constant in width, like a laser-etched trace, and the retro friendliness comes from that single steady stroke. Noto Sans Old Sogdian is the practical partner, with a lofty x-height and wide-mouthed letters that stay crisp when shrunk.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-old-tur: Chunky, open and cheerful, Noto Sans Old Turkic keeps its curves clear with big mouths and sturdy lowercase. And Junegull sets it off with closed, retro letters, horizontals as heavy as verticals, which is the pair's real hook.
